subject: history_social
passage: Before 1914, a ship sailing from New York to San Francisco had to travel all the way around the southern tip of South America, a voyage of more than 20,000 kilometers. That year, the Panama Canal opened across a narrow strip of land in Central America, connecting the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Ships could now pass between the two oceans without going around the continent. As a result, the voyage from New York to San Francisco most likely became ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: longer, because ships now had to wait to enter the canal.
choices.B: possible by sea for the first time in history.
choices.C: much shorter than it had been before the canal opened.
choices.D: unnecessary, because the canal linked the two cities directly.

explanation.why: Before the canal, ships had to sail around South America. The canal let them cross between the oceans through Central America instead, which cut out that long detour and made the trip much shorter.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text gives no information about waiting times, and avoiding a 20,000-kilometer detour would shorten the trip.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says ships already made this voyage before 1914 by going around South America.
explanation.C: Correct. Skipping the trip around South America would greatly shorten the voyage.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The canal crosses Central America; it does not connect New York and San Francisco directly.
